text:
elaine: Heads-up: prepping private EU rollout. Need quick decision: allowlist KMS IPs in NetworkPolicy or enforce egress via an egress-gateway? Pros/cons?

rob: Egress gateway is safer operationally (rotating IPs, cert pinning), but adds infra. If timeline tight, temporary IP allowlist + short TTL certs.

mike: RBAC note: keystore-agent should run with a namespaced SA and Role that only allows `secrets/get` for named secrets and `pods/exec` false. No cluster roles. Also bind key policy on KMS to the SA OIDC subject.

elaine: Audit question 024: need tamper-evident audit chain. Thoughts on signing entries vs. merkle root?

rob: Do both if possible: sign each entry (ed25519) and publish hourly Merkle root to immutable bucket. Forward signed logs to SIEM via mTLS.

sec-bot: [automated] SEC-3301 created for deployment hardening. Assignee: rob.

infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: pipelines/private-rollout/keystore-protect-1759999999 -> canary at 2024-12-05T08:00Z.

mike: If CVEs present, plan: patch image, rotate SA tokens, restrict netpol to canary nodes, run decrypt audit for last 24h.

elaine: OK landing plan: egress-gateway preferred; fallback to IP allowlist for first 48h. Will update runbook and OPA policy to block wide egress.

rob: I'll draft envoy bootstrap and OPA constraint in a PR.

elaine: Thanks, team. Results expected within 3 hours of canary.
